chunks: Muḥammad ibn Abī ʿUmayr narrated from ʿAbdullāh ibn Sinān, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:
A man from the Anṣār, during the time of the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله, went out for some of his needs and instructed his wife not to leave her house until he returned.

He said: Her father became ill, so the woman sent to the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله and said: My husband has gone out and instructed me not to leave my house until he returns, and my father is ill, so do you command me to visit him? He said: No, stay in your house and obey your husband.

He said: Then he died, so she sent to him and said: O Messenger of Allah, my father has died, so do you command me to perform the funeral prayer over him? He said: No, stay in your house and obey your husband.

He said: Then the man was buried, and the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله sent to her: Indeed Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has forgiven you and your father because of your obedience to your husband.

key_terms.أَطِيعِي: obey; the Prophet’s command to comply with the husband
key_terms.الْأَنْصَارِ: the Anṣār, the Helpers of Madinah from whom the man in the report was
key_terms.حَوَائِجِهِ: his needs or errands for which he went out
key_terms.زَوْجَكِ: your husband, whose right is central in the report
key_terms.عَهْدًا: a charge or firm instruction given by the husband
key_terms.غَفَرَ: forgave; indicating divine pardon granted in the narration

ai.seo_question: What does this hadith say about a wife's obedience to her husband when her father is ill or dies?
ai.summary: This hadith narrates the account of an Anṣārī woman who remained in her home in obedience to her husband’s instruction, even when her father became ill and then died. The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله affirmed her obedience, and the report concludes with divine forgiveness for her and her father because of that obedience.
